assertions.notes: POST /reservations -> 201 with a booked online reservation, 8-char Crockford code and a manageToken; the sqlite row carries the hold id and client=web and the hold flipped to converted; a second conversion with the same hold token -> 410 hold_expired.

Byte-identical replay with the same Idempotency-Key -> 201, same reservation id and code, identical manage token (sha match); the same key with a changed firstName -> 409 idempotency_conflict; the guest still has exactly one reservation row.

Slot 17:30 was reduced to a single party-8 unit (G10-T12) by blocking Main Dining (the m3+m4 combo) and occupying G10-T1..T6, T11 with staff bookings; the guest hold took tbl_71be1db7-93f8-42d4-be22-96dab1fe4720; a staff booking on the held table with overbook:true -> 201; the guest conversion then returned 409 slot_unavailable with alternatives (sameDay,otherDates), created no reservation (rows for that phone: 0) and left the hold active.
assertions.limitations: The single-unit slot was constructed with isolation blocks/staff bookings rather than finding an already-exhausted slot; the control case (conversion succeeding without a staff overbook) is VAL-ONLINE-013 on the same date.

assertions.notes: X-Client ios and android both produced channel=native with client=ios / client=android in rsv_reservations; the X-Client: web booking of VAL-ONLINE-013 stayed channel=online, client=web.

frictions: The public book/hold routes are behind a durable per-IP bucket (book_ip 20/day, holds_ip 10/10min). Every local client hashes to the same literal IP, so parallel groups exhaust one shared bucket; private X-Forwarded-For values avoid it.
